comments.text: Initializes each fighter's $781A/$781B value to 200 minus its training byte at $CE17/$CE18, modulo 256. Selects separate initialization paths for one and two apprentices using $CE00.
Restores VIC-II settings, sets video bank $0000 and selects the $0400 screen and $2000 bitmap. Calls $EC68 with the scene index and chooses the outcome or fight setup using $CD59.

Selects the descriptor bank using the facing flag at $780E and looks up the pose through $7DCF. Adds $B500 to the relative pointer and distributes eight or sixteen bytes to the alternating display buffers.
Reads the name at $7896 up to $FF. Converts each byte to a glyph offset in RAM beneath I/O and copies its eight pixel rows into the bitmap beginning at $2000.
Stages the first fighter index and facing flag before jumping to the common shape address calculation.
Stages the second fighter index and its own facing flag, and then jumps to the same shape address calculation.

Builds the output pointer from the supplied position and backing-plane offsets. Looks up the shape through a relative word at $8000 and uses its two dimension bytes before dispatching to the appropriate painter.
Selects the blend path according to facing. Applies the pixel mask lookup when combining the packed fighter rows with the destination.
Selects the row copying path according to the second fighter facing bit. Advances the bitmap destination by $140 per row and the source by the packed row width.
Clears the bitmap destination at $2000 and the auxiliary plane beginning at $5180 using overlapping page writes.

Indexes the ten-byte descriptors at $7832 with the scene index in A. Reads the stream backwards and handles literal, run, pointer reset and exit tokens. Writes the selected bitmap and screen-colour plane.
Banks out ROM and I/O to read the source at ($58),Y. Decrements the 16-bit input pointer, restores the ROM mapping and preserves X.
Banks out ROM and I/O to write A through ($5A),Y. Decrements the 16-bit output pointer and restores the ROM mapping.
Copies the first row from $78BF and the lower rows from $4C40 and $4C54. Fills the colour RAM and initializes the screen and work copies of the lower display.

Blanks the screen, mutes the SID, restores the ROM and KERNAL vectors and loads HIGH from device 8 before returning to BASIC run.
The four-byte name HIGH passed to KERNAL SETNAM by the combat exit.
At raster $FF, sets border and background to black and blanks the display. Returns after 100 successful reads of raster line zero.
Waits for raster line zero and sets $D011 to $3B to enable the bitmap display.
Sets the KERNAL input and output device numbers to 0 and 3. Copies the VIC-II preset from $ECB9, leaving display control, border and background colour unchanged.

The three-page glyph source for the combat introduction, read from the RAM beneath I/O and copied to the character generator at $2000.
Waits for CIA1 port A to equal $6F. A different reading clears the latch at $CE23, and accepting a press sets the latch so a held button cannot count twice.
Clears the screen, builds the bordered interlude from the shared templates at $CF00 and chooses its text through $CD4D. Shows it until fire, then blanks the display.
Selects a sequence of text IDs through $EE4A. Passes each to $ECFF until encountering $FF.
Selects a message pointer through $EE6D, uses its row and column to find screen RAM, translates capital letters to screen codes and handles $FE and $FF delimiters.
Places character RAM at $2000 and the matrix at $0400. Banks out I/O while reading the font at $DC80 and then programs the display colours.
